Prosecution story, in brief is that the applicant is husband of the 2 MCRC-22890-2024 complainant Nidhi.
Their marriage was performed on 10.05.2022.
After the marriage, the present applicant and co-accused/mother-in-law of the complainant Vimla Gupta used to torture the complainant physically and mentally for small domestic issues.
On 08.04.2024, there was quarrel between the complainant and accused persons.

Meanwhile, the accused persons abused the Rohit Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39969569/

sentences.text: The accused persons snatched her mobile phone and chain and they forcibly made her drink some poisonous substance.
Thereafter, the complainant ran to her maternal home and they took her to hospital for treatment.
A telephonic intimation about the incident received from Hospital, a Rojnamchasanha was recorded and after enquiry, an FIR was lodged on 13.04.2024.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant has not tortured the complainant physically or mentally.
She herself left the house of the applicant and false report has been lodged by her.
The applicant is a reputed person.
Police is trying to arrest him.
If he gets arrested, his reputation will be tarnished, therefore, it is prayed that he may be granted anticipatory bail.

5. On other hand learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that first anticipatory bail of the applicant has been dismissed as withdrawn with the liberty to surrender before the trial Court/Competent Court and the trial Court/Competent Court was directed to consider his application for regular bail as expeditiously as possible.
It is also submitted that apart from that the applicant has not surrender before the trial Court/Competent Court and repeat application has been filed by him.
Custodial interrogation of the applicant is required, therefore he is not entitled for 3 MCRC-22890-2024 anticipatory bail.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in view of this Court, at this stage, it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, application for grant of anticipatory bail is rejected.
